name: Discharge of an adult medical inpatient from an acute hospital
function: inpatient nursing, care management and patient flow
summary: Discharging a medical inpatient starts with a discharge planning assessment early in the stay and ends when the bed is cleaned and released for the next patient. Case managers and social workers arrange home health or facility placement and payer approvals, the hospitalist writes the order, reconciles medications and the discharge summary, and the nurse teaches the patient and family before transport. Much of the work is at the bedside and on the phone. Delays come from waiting for facility bed offers and plan approvals, late discharge orders, nurse availability, rides that arrive late and rooms waiting for cleaning, and errors in medication lists and follow-up plans lead to harm and readmissions after discharge.

baseline.org_archetype: A US community hospital of about 300 beds with a hospitalist group, RN case managers and social workers, and in-house pharmacy, therapy, transport and environmental services.
baseline.notes: Adult medical (non-surgical) inpatients discharged alive; transfers to another acute hospital, deaths and discharges against medical advice are out of scope. Post-discharge phone calls are also out of scope.

trigger: An adult patient is admitted to a medical unit and enters the discharge planning screen.
end_state: The patient has left with instructions, medications, follow-up and any post-acute services arranged, and the bed is cleaned and released.

volume.seasonality: Higher in winter respiratory season; discharges cluster on weekdays and are fewer on weekends.

evidence.note: Estimate: 300 beds at about 75 percent occupancy and 4.5-day stays give about 1,500 discharges a month, of which about 60 percent are medical; HCUP reports medical stays at 56 percent of all stays.

triggered_by.from: Inpatient admission (emergency department and direct admissions)

produces.to: Bed management and emergency department admissions
Primary care physician and receiving facility or home health agency
Health information management coding and billing

systems.name: Hospital electronic health record (orders, notes, medication reconciliation, discharge instructions)
Admission, discharge and transfer system and electronic bed board
Care management documentation and post-acute referral portal
Dictation and transcription (or EHR note templates)
Printed forms and notices (discharge instructions, appeal notice, transfer packet)

steps.name: Screen and assess discharge needs
steps.description: Within a day or two of admission the RN case manager reviews the chart, interviews the patient and family about home situation, prior services, insurance and caregivers, scores readmission and post-acute risk, and documents an initial discharge plan in the care management system.

error.defect_description: Post-acute need or home barrier not identified, found late in the stay.

control.basis: 42 CFR 482.43(a): identify at an early stage patients likely to need discharge planning; evaluation by or under an RN, social worker or other qualified person.

evidence.note: Requirement from the CoP; timing, touch time and Medicare share are estimates.

steps.name: Deliver the Important Message from Medicare
steps.description: Staff take the standard Medicare discharge appeal rights notice to the bedside, explain it, and have the patient or representative sign and date it; the signed copy is scanned into the record.

error.defect_description: Notice not delivered within 2 days or unsigned.

control.basis: 42 CFR 405.1205(b): deliver the standardized notice within 2 calendar days of admission with signature.

evidence.note: Timing rule stated in the regulation; touch time is an estimate. Delivered during the treatment days, so its wait overlaps the wait before rounds.

steps.name: Physical therapy evaluates mobility and disposition
steps.description: A physical therapist assesses transfers, gait and stairs at the bedside, reviews the home setup with the patient, and writes a recommendation for home, home with services and equipment, or a skilled nursing or rehabilitation facility.

error.defect_description: Recommendation changes on re-evaluation, reopening the plan.

evidence.note: Common practice for older medical inpatients; share and times are estimates. Runs during the treatment days, so its queue overlaps the wait before rounds.

steps.name: Interdisciplinary rounds confirm readiness and disposition
steps.description: Each day the hospitalist, nurse and case manager review progress, set the expected discharge date and the disposition, and identify barriers such as pending tests or consults. The wait before this step is the remaining treatment time until the patient is medically ready.

error.defect_description: Expected date set without the barriers resolved, causing a late-day cancellation.

next.condition: home with home health or equipment
skilled nursing, rehabilitation or other facility

evidence.note: HCUP mean stay 4.5 days; disposition shares for adult medical patients are estimates.

steps.name: Arrange home health and equipment
steps.description: The case manager gives the patient the list of participating home health agencies, records the choice, sends the referral with orders and face-to-face documentation through the referral portal or fax, and orders equipment such as a walker or home oxygen from a supplier.

error.defect_description: Missing orders or documentation; agency asks again.

control.basis: 42 CFR 482.43(c): list of participating home health agencies, patient freedom of choice and no steering.

evidence.note: Choice-list rule from the CoP; times are estimates.

steps.name: Home health agency accepts and schedules the first visit
steps.description: The agency's intake team checks coverage, staffing for the patient's area and the orders, then accepts and sets a start-of-care date, or declines.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Acceptance time and decline share are estimates.

steps.name: Present facility choices and send referrals
steps.description: The social worker meets the patient and family, gives the list of participating skilled nursing or rehabilitation facilities with quality data, records their choices, and sends referral packets with clinical notes, therapy notes and medication lists to several facilities through the referral portal.

error.defect_description: Referral packet incomplete; facility asks for more before deciding.

control.basis: 42 CFR 482.43(c): list of participating SNF, IRF or LTCH providers with quality and resource-use data, patient choice respected and no limiting of providers.

evidence.note: Choice-list and quality-data rule from the CoP; times are estimates.

steps.name: Facilities review referrals and offer beds
steps.description: Admissions staff at each facility review the clinical packet, insurance and care needs and decide whether to offer a bed and when; families may tour before choosing.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: bed offered; traditional Medicare, no authorization

evidence.note: Traditional Medicare needs a qualifying 3-day stay but no prior authorization; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Request authorization for the post-acute stay
steps.description: The case manager submits clinical notes and therapy evaluations to the Medicare Advantage or commercial plan through its portal or by fax and answers questions from the plan's reviewer.

error.defect_description: Missing therapy notes lead to a pend.

control.basis: Health plan prior authorization requirement for post-acute admissions (plan contract and medical policy).

evidence.note: OIG found post-acute stays among prior authorization denials that met Medicare rules; times are estimates.

steps.name: Plan decides on the post-acute request
steps.description: The plan's utilization review nurse and medical director review the request; the patient stays in the hospital bed while the decision is pending.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

next.condition: denied; home with home health instead

evidence.note: Shares and decision time are estimates.

steps.name: Write the discharge order and reconcile medications
steps.description: The hospitalist writes the discharge order, compares the home medication list with inpatient orders in the EHR reconciliation screen, decides which drugs to continue, stop or change, signs new prescriptions and lists follow-up needs.

error.defect_description: Medication discrepancy or error in instructions.

control.basis: Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goal NPSG.03.06.01: compare current and ordered medications, resolve discrepancies and give the patient the list.

evidence.note: About 1 in 10 discharges had instruction or medication errors or near-misses; times are estimates.

steps.name: Pharmacist reviews the discharge medication list
steps.description: For patients on many or high-risk drugs, the pharmacist checks the reconciled list for omissions, duplicates and interactions, contacts the hospitalist about discrepancies and counsels the patient at the bedside.

error.defect_description: A discrepancy is missed.

control.basis: Hospital policy for pharmacist review of high-risk discharges.

evidence.note: Pharmacist-led reconciliation prevents discrepancies; selection share and times are estimates.

steps.name: Write the discharge summary
steps.description: The hospitalist dictates or types the discharge summary with the hospital course, final diagnoses, disposition, medication changes, pending results and follow-up plan, and signs it; it is sent to the primary care physician and any receiving facility. Many summaries are finished after the patient leaves.

error.defect_description: Pending results or medication changes left out, or summary sent late.

control.basis: 42 CFR 482.24(c)(4)(vii) and (viii): discharge summary with outcome, disposition and follow-up, and records completed within 30 days; 42 CFR 482.43 transfer of necessary information.

evidence.note: Summaries often do not reach outpatient physicians in time; touch time is an estimate.

steps.name: Give the follow-up copy of the Medicare notice
steps.description: The case manager or unit staff give the patient a copy of the signed appeal rights notice no more than two days before discharge and answer questions; a patient who appeals stays while the quality improvement organization reviews.

error.defect_description: Copy not given within the window.

control.basis: 42 CFR 405.1205(c): follow-up copy no more than 2 calendar days before discharge.

evidence.note: Timing rule from the regulation; times are estimates.

steps.name: Nurse removes lines and teaches the discharge plan
steps.description: The staff nurse removes the IV and monitors, prints the discharge instructions, goes through medications, warning signs and follow-up with the patient and family using teach-back, gets signatures and returns belongings. The nurse fits this between other patients' care.

error.defect_description: Patient leaves without understanding medication changes.

control.basis: Hospital discharge education policy (teach-back and signed instructions), supporting the CoP requirement to involve patients and caregivers.

next.condition: discharge cancelled: clinical change or patient not ready

evidence.note: Teach-back and checklists per PSNet; about a third of patients need more education; times are estimates.

steps.name: Book follow-up appointments
steps.description: The unit clerk calls the primary care or specialist office to book a visit within one to two weeks and writes the date on the instructions; when offices are closed the patient is told to call.

error.defect_description: No appointment made; patient told to schedule.

evidence.note: Up to half of patients told to schedule follow-up may not; times are estimates.

steps.name: Arrange the ride
steps.description: The unit clerk or case manager confirms who is picking the patient up, or books a wheelchair van or ambulance for patients going to a facility or who cannot travel by car.

error.defect_description: Wrong pick-up time given.

evidence.note: Common practice; shares and times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the family to arrive
steps.description: The patient waits in the room, or in a discharge lounge where one exists, until the family member arrives after work or school.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Give report and send the transfer packet
steps.description: For facility transfers the nurse phones a report to the receiving nurse and prints or sends the transfer packet with the summary, medication list and orders; for medical transport the packet goes with the crew.

error.defect_description: Packet missing the medication list or summary.

control.basis: 42 CFR 482.43(b): transfer the patient with all necessary medical information to the post-acute provider.

evidence.note: Information-transfer rule from the CoP; times are estimates.

steps.name: Wait for the wheelchair van or ambulance
steps.description: The transport company sends a crew at the booked time, often later, and the patient stays in the bed until it arrives.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Estimate.

steps.name: Escort the patient out
steps.description: A transporter or nursing assistant brings a wheelchair, takes the patient and belongings to the exit or to the ambulance crew, and confirms departure with the nurse.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Record the discharge in the ADT system
steps.description: The unit clerk enters the discharge time and disposition in the ADT system, which marks the bed dirty on the bed board and sends a cleaning request to environmental services. Entry is often delayed when the clerk is busy.

error.defect_description: Wrong disposition code entered.

evidence.note: Common practice; delay is an estimate.

steps.name: Clean the room after discharge
steps.description: An environmental services technician takes the task from the dispatch system, strips the bed, removes waste and linen, cleans and disinfects surfaces and equipment, and remakes the bed; isolation rooms need a longer clean.

error.defect_description: Surface or equipment missed.

control.basis: Infection prevention and control standards for environmental cleaning (Joint Commission infection control chapter and hospital policy).

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

steps.name: Inspect and release the bed
steps.description: The environmental services lead or charge nurse checks the room, then marks the bed clean on the bed board so bed placement can assign the next patient from the emergency department or admissions queue.

error.defect_description: None introduced.

control.basis: Hospital environmental services quality inspection policy.

evidence.note: Common practice; times are estimates.

exceptions.name: Skilled nursing or rehabilitation placement
exceptions.description: Referrals to several facilities, waiting for bed offers and, for managed care, plan authorization, while the patient occupies the bed.

exceptions.name: Plan denies post-acute stay
exceptions.description: The plan denies; the team requests a peer-to-peer and resubmits, or arranges home health instead.

exceptions.name: Discharge cancelled on the day
exceptions.description: A new symptom, test result or unready family stops the discharge after the order and education.

exceptions.name: Medicare appeal of discharge
exceptions.description: The patient asks the quality improvement organization to review the discharge and stays until it decides.

exceptions.name: Medical transport delay
exceptions.description: Facility and non-ambulatory patients wait for a wheelchair van or ambulance crew.

exceptions.name: Agency declines home health referral
exceptions.description: The agency lacks staff for the area and the case manager refers to another.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the discharge planning screen to the bed released (about the length of stay)
benchmarks.population: Adult medical inpatients, US community hospitals

evidence.note: HCUP reports a mean stay of 4.5 days for all US stays in 2012; the median for medical stays is lower than the mean, and the 90th percentile is an estimate.

benchmarks.unit: share of Medicare patients readmitted within 30 days (nearly 20 percent)

benchmarks.population: Classic study cited by AHRQ PSNet

benchmarks.unit: share of discharges (about 1 in 10, including caught near-misses)
benchmarks.population: One study cited by AHRQ PSNet

pain_points.description: Patients who are medically ready wait in beds for facility bed offers and plan authorizations.

evidence.note: Waiting durations are estimates.

pain_points.description: Discharge day is hard to predict, so orders, education and information all happen in a rush on the day.
Medication discrepancies and missing follow-up lead to harm after discharge.
Discharge summaries often reach the outpatient physician late or lack pending results.
Late rides, delayed ADT entries and cleaning queues hold the bed empty while emergency patients wait for it.

evidence.note: Common patient-flow problem; estimate.

sources.title: 42 CFR 482.43 Condition of participation: Discharge planning
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Hospitals must identify at an early stage patients likely to need discharge planning, have an RN, social worker or qualified person do or supervise the evaluation, give patients going to home health, SNF, IRF or LTCH a list of participating providers with quality and resource-use data without steering, involve patients and caregivers, and send all necessary medical information to the receiving provider.

sources.title: 42 CFR 405.1205 Notifying beneficiaries of hospital discharge appeal rights
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: The standardized notice must be delivered within 2 calendar days of admission and signed; a follow-up copy is given no more than 2 calendar days before discharge unless the first notice fell within that window.

sources.title: 42 CFR 482.24 Condition of participation: Medical record services
sources.publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
sources.supports: Records must contain a discharge summary with outcome, disposition and follow-up provisions, and a final diagnosis, with records completed within 30 days after discharge; entries must be dated, timed and authenticated.

sources.title: Readmissions and Adverse Events After Discharge (PSNet primer)
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Patient Safety Network
sources.supports: About 20% of patients have an adverse event within 3 weeks of discharge; nearly 20% of Medicare patients are readmitted within 30 days; nearly 40% leave with results pending; discharge summaries often do not reach outpatient physicians in time; medication reconciliation, structured communication, education and multifaceted programs such as Project RED.

sources.title: Medication Reconciliation (PSNet primer)
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Patient Safety Network
sources.supports: Medication reconciliation has been part of Joint Commission National Patient Safety Goal 3 since 2011; pharmacist-led reconciliation prevents discrepancies; it takes considerable time and resources; technicians are used to reduce cost.

sources.title: Discharge Planning and Transitions of Care (PSNet primer)
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, Patient Safety Network
sources.supports: About 1 in 10 discharges had errors in instructions or medications or a caught near-miss; about a third of patients need more education; up to half told to schedule follow-up may not; discharge day is hard to predict so information is given that day; teach-back, checklists, follow-up booked before discharge; pharmacist and nurse roles.

sources.title: Hospital Readmissions Reduction Program (HRRP)
sources.supports: Medicare reduces payments by up to 3 percent for excess 30-day readmissions for AMI, COPD, heart failure, pneumonia, CABG and hip or knee replacement, since FY2013.

sources.title: Skilled nursing facility (SNF) care coverage
sources.supports: Medicare SNF coverage needs a medically necessary inpatient stay of at least 3 days in a row (observation does not count), SNF admission generally within 30 days and daily skilled care; some MA plans waive the 3-day rule.

sources.title: Overview of Hospital Stays in the United States, 2012 (HCUP Statistical Brief 180)
sources.publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality, HCUP
sources.supports: 36.5 million stays in 2012, average length of stay 4.5 days, mean cost $10,400; medical stays 56% of all stays.

sources.title: Some Medicare Advantage Organization Denials of Prior Authorization Requests Raise Concerns About Beneficiary Access to Medically Necessary Care (OEI-09-18-00260)
sources.supports: Post-acute facility stays such as inpatient rehabilitation were among the prior authorization denials that met Medicare coverage rules (13% of sampled denials).

sources.title: Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics, May 2021 National Estimates
sources.supports: Mean hourly wages May 2021: registered nurses $39.78, healthcare social workers $29.96, general internal medicine physicians $116.44, pharmacists $60.43, medical secretaries and administrative assistants $19.11, orderlies $16.08, maids and housekeeping cleaners $14.22, nursing assistants $15.99, ambulance drivers and attendants $14.93.

sources.title: Employer Costs for Employee Compensation, December 2021
sources.supports: Private hospitals: wages 66.1% of compensation, benefits 33.9%.

assumptions: The wait before interdisciplinary rounds stands for the remaining treatment time until the patient is medically ready, not a queue; it dominates the cycle time.
Disposition shares for adult medical inpatients (65 percent home with self-care, 18 percent home health, 17 percent facility) are estimates; no source for this population was opened.
About 48 percent of medical inpatients are Medicare beneficiaries and receive the appeal-rights notice twice; estimate.
Order-to-departure and departure-to-clean-bed times are estimates from general practice; no time-and-motion study was opened.
Hands-on minutes count only discharge-related work, not the clinical care given during the stay.
Discharge summaries are drawn as running alongside education because many are signed after the patient leaves, within the 30-day record completion rule.

Fte_on_process values are the share of each role's time spent on discharge work for these patients, from hands-on time times volume at 130 productive hours a month plus an allowance for travel between rooms and documentation outside the steps.
